title: Trading card printed as a cyanotype specimen sheet, four rarities by process: paper edge, silver frame, tannin field with copper foil, full deep field on gold foil
use: A trading card face (2.5 x 3.5 in at 300 dpi) in four rarities with --param rarity=common|rare|epic|legend; the specimen goes in the art slot as white lines with alpha, as a cyanotype prints it.

rarity.note: the rarity sets the process: common paper edge, rare silver frame, epic tannin-toned field and copper foil, legend full deep field, gold foil, name on a gold label and the rules on a tilted paper label

field_seed.note: seed of the hand-brushed field's edge and streaks

art.note: the specimen as white lines on transparency (materials cut --finish ink, then the style's cyanotype recipe); a drawn algae frond stands in until it is filled

rules.default: 入匣时：双方场上所有寻常标本洗回牌库。

flavor.default: 匣中唯一一件，没有人见过第二只。

credit.default: 原图 作者 · 年代 · 公有领域
credit.note: credit the public-domain print you used

relations: One Prussian blue for every card; rarity is a different process, never a different hue (only epic is toned, with tannin).
The specimen is a white shadow on the blue field, centred in the field; text stays on the solid part of the field, away from the brushed edge (the edge is where contrast drops).
Rules on paper below the field; stats bottom left, collector and credit bottom right, 14 px.
decoration: Brushed field edge and streaks, flat guilloche foil, silver corner brackets, rarity sigils (circle, lozenge, hexagram, rayed sun), the keyword icon.

provenance.corpus: card-game case (藏珍匣 RARIUM): our own original fictional trading card game in the cyanotype-specimen grammar
provenance.experiment: styles/cyanotype-specimen/style.json provenance; case renders in docs/cases/card-game
provenance.method: Positions from the case's card.css (750 x 1050) for all four rarities; the brushed field (case fields.py, a raster) is redrawn as a jittered polygon with bristle streaks; the foil guilloche as in cards.js.
measured: First pass 10 / 20 / 21 / 15 findings on four cards: the paper and field textures were normal-blended images and counted as collage under text (fixed by multiplying them), and cost, name and type sat on the brushed edge at 1.9:1 (margins 26 to 14 px, text moved onto the solid field); final 0 on all nine cards.
The legend's griffin head breaking the top edge needs a separate cut-out (the case's griffin-pop.png); this template keeps the art inside the field.
